documents.name: GitHub
documents.description: Integrate with GitHub and receive related events
documents.instructions:
### Enable

To enable this integration, you will be asked:
- to accept the GitHub App permissions, and
- select a GitHub organisation to install into.

Once you have installed the app, you will be redirected back to complete the integration by choosing which team to link the app to.

### Disable

To disable this integration, you can either
- remove the GitHub App installation from your GitHub organisation, or
- unlink the app by reopening this integration modal and selecting 'disable'

documents.name: Slack
documents.description: Run workflows from Slack, and let the Slack tasks post and manage channels as the Flow app
documents.instructions:
### Enable

To enable this integration, you will be asked to:
- choose the Slack workspace to install the Flow app into, and
- allow the app's permissions.

Once Slack has installed the app, you are returned here with Slack connected to this workspace. Several Flow workspaces can connect the same Slack workspace.

The app asks Slack for these bot scopes:
- `chat:write`, `commands`, `users:read` and `users:read.email` - the slash command that runs a workflow, and the find member tasks
- `channels:read` and `groups:read` - the get channel tasks
- `channels:manage` and `groups:write` - the create, delete, invite and remove channel tasks
- `files:write` - the upload file task

### Disable

To disable this integration, you can either
- disconnect it here, which removes it from this Flow workspace only, or
- remove the Flow app from your Slack workspace, which disconnects every Flow workspace using it

fields.name: slack-token
fields.label: Slack token
fields.description: The Flow app's bot token for the connected Slack workspace
